title: Write layout checks against the template
statement: Write any check that depends on where things sit against a shared template, never against one example's arrangement, or it won't carry to the next one.
example: Twelve lesson-level checks were written, and not one has been named that would carry to a lesson in a course it wasn't built for.
detail: The evaluator's lesson-level checks were written against one reference course, so each structural variation needed bespoke handling instead of a repeatable rubric, and of twelve such checks not one has been named that would carry to a course it was not built for. The team agreed to adopt a template per content type and to rebuild the lesson checks against it rather than extend them from the reference course. The test it set itself: a check written for one course's lessons fires on a defect in a lesson from a different course built to the same template.
against: The source records objections from both sides: that 'a bespoke check that catches a real defect today is worth more than a portable check that does not exist yet', and that 'form should follow the learning goal, and giving a vocabulary page and a problem set the same template flattens real differences between subjects' (shadow-bench/docs/brainlift.md line 125). The claim is not yet earned: '*Weakest point:* the two lanes are still not a clean experiment.' (line 132).
